issues.author: Mike Lothian
issues.description:
## Hardware

- ASUS ROG Strix G513QY, BIOS G513QY.335
- Navi 22 dGPU (03:00.0) behind its on-package PCIe switch, iGPU on GP17
- USB-C DP alt mode port wired to the dGPU

## Problem

With the dGPU in D3cold, attaching a USB-C dock raises GPE 0x05 and logs:

```
ACPI BIOS Error (bug): Could not resolve symbol [\_SB.PCI0.GPP0.VGA], AE_NOT_FOUND
ACPI Error: Aborting method \_GPE._L05 due to previous error (AE_NOT_FOUND)
ACPI Error: AE_NOT_FOUND, while evaluating GPE method [_L05]
```

The dGPU stays off, no hotplug reaches userspace and the external displays stay dark.
`acpi_mask_gpe=0x05` hides the errors but also removes the hotplug.

## Cause, as far as the tables show

`_L05` is in the AMD CPM D3cold table (SSDT9, OEM table id `CPMD3CLD`) and is just
`Notify (\_SB.PCI0.GPP0.VGA, 0x81)`. On this board the dGPU is
`\_SB.PCI0.GPP0.SWUS.SWDS.VGA_`, so the Notify target does not exist.

The iGPU is `\_SB.PCI0.GP17.VGA_` and carries ATIF/ATCS (SSDT6 and SSDT7), so ATIF is
bound to the iGPU only and nothing listens on the dGPU's own node.

## Workarounds tried

1. An SSDT that aliases `\_SB.PCI0.GPP0.VGA` to the real node (loaded through
   `CONFIG_ACPI_TABLE_UPGRADE`) gets the Notify delivered. With an amdgpu notify handler on
   the dGPU's ACPI companion the dock then lights up.
2. A DMI-matched GPE handler in amdgpu that replaces `_L05` when the Notify target does not
   resolve. It works with no table override.

Both are in the amd-gfx series "[PATCH 0/2] drm/amdgpu: wake a pow

issues.title: [DCN 4.0.1] PREEMPT_RT: scheduling while atomic in dc_create_plane_state() from dml21 phantom plane path → panic
issues.author: Sebastian Paul
issues.description:
## Brief summary of the problem:

On a PREEMPT_RT kernel, the system hard-locks (or panics, with panic settings enabled) when a
fullscreen game on one monitor regains focus after a window on the other monitor was active.
SubVP re-evaluation creates a phantom plane inside `dcn401_validate_bandwidth()`'s DC_FP region,
and `dc_create_plane_state()` calls `kvzalloc_obj()` there. On PREEMPT_RT the page allocator's zone
lock is a sleeping lock, so the worker sleeps while atomic. It migrates (CPU 31 → 8),
`fpu_recursion_depth` goes negative, and the later `vfree` in `dml21_destroy()` hits
`BUG_ON(in_nmi())` at mm/vmalloc.c:3428.

Three lockups on the first day of 7.3. 7.2.x ran for days on the same setup without one.

The fix is posted but unmerged: Bert Karwatzki, "drm/amd/display: fix usage of DC_FPU_{BEGIN,END}
with PREEMPT_RT" (amd-gfx, v4 2026-08-07, Fixes: 3539437f354b). I applied the equivalent locally,
plus wrapping `dc_stream_release()`/`dc_plane_state_release()` in
`dc_state_release_phantom_stream()`/`_plane()`. With that, five days, 98 h of uptime and daily
gaming sessions with the same focus switching produced no lockup and no DC_FP warning. As of
2026-10-29, `dc_create_plane_state()` is still unguarded in mainline (after the 7.4 DRM merge) and in
amd-staging-drm-next.

issues.title: drm/amdkfd: Stale KFD queues after GPU reset can trigger cascading resets
issues.author: Daniel Huang
issues.description:
## Summary

KFD queue teardown appears unable to execute during GPU reset because of a reset-domain lock conflict:

* `amdgpu_device_gpu_recover()` holds `reset_domain->sem` for writing.
* `remove_queue_mes()` attempts `down_read_trylock()` on the same semaphore and immediately returns `-EIO`.
* As a result, pre-reset teardown never reaches MES. This was confirmed with kprobes across two independent hangs.

The more significant issue appears to be **incomplete post-reset queue recovery**. `kgd2kfd_post_reset()` resumes KFD without reconciling queues that could not be removed. These queues remain valid in KFD's bookkeeping but may no longer exist in firmware.

A subsequent queue operation, including implicit removal during process exit, can fail and invoke `kfd_hws_hang()`, triggering another GPU reset. In one reproduction, the GPU remained unusable until reboot.

This was discovered while investigating [ROCm/TheRock#8357](https://github.com/ROCm/TheRock/issues/8357) (gfx90c/HWS). The same locking mechanism was reproduced on gfx1103/MES.

### Brief summary of the problem

wakes from DPMS off. On 7.2 the driver aborts the stream enable, the MST branch

issues.title: Hard lockup in dmub_srv_wait_for_idle via IPS exit from drm_vblank_enable (DCN 3.5, Strix Point)
issues.author: Alexandre DUVAL
issues.description:
## Summary

On a Strix Point (Radeon 890M, DCN 3.5) laptop, the machine hard-freezes every one
to two days. A pstore dump from one of these freezes shows a **kernel panic — Hard
LOCKUP** with the CPU stuck in `delay_halt` inside `dmub_srv_wait_for_idle()`,
reached from the IPS-exit path that `dm_read_reg_func()` triggers while reading a
display register.

The critical detail is the context: this busy-wait is entered from
`drm_vblank_get()` → `drm_vblank_enable()`, which holds `dev->vbl_lock` with
**interrupts disabled**. The register dump confirms it — `EFLAGS: 00000807`, IF
(0x200) clear. So when DMUB fails to report idle, the CPU spins forever with IRQs
off, which is why this manifests as an NMI hard lockup and a dead machine rather
than a recoverable stall or a soft lockup.

`amdgpu.dcdebugmask=0x800` (`DC_DISABLE_IPS`) is an effective workaround.

```
issues.author: Furkan Kara
issues.description:
# amdgpu/DP MST: payload start slot leaks after HPD-loss topology teardown, hub is given PAYLOAD_ALLOCATE_START_TIME_SLOT \> 63, daisy-chained monitors stay black and re-train every 15 s (DCN 3.5, Krackan)

[full_drm_debug_capture.log](/uploads/19f5365b624db904074d4b3d96958ebc/full_drm_debug_capture.log)

# 

[mst_start_stop_all_boot.log](/uploads/9e1e49adc889f53f4c8445ecc3007ee5/mst_start_stop_all_boot.log)

# 

[one_cycle_drm_debug_0x116_trimmed.log](/uploads/14ccce8d3f39097b4c65d28b7533bd0b/one_cycle_drm_debug_0x116_trimmed.log)

# 

[replug_warnings_12-06.log](/uploads/e2ccfdad3e2a0f4550a79d177df0a329/replug_warnings_12-06.log)

## Summary

With a USB-C DisplayPort MST daisy chain (Philips 27B2U4601 hub → Philips 27M1N3200ZA), both external monitors go black and the MST topology is torn down and rebuilt on a fixed cycle (14.98 s up, 3.57 s down), indefinitely. The link itself is healthy (HBR3 x2 trains every time, DRM's bandwidth check passes, both sinks enumerate). The failure is in the payload table the source writes to the hub: with `drm.debug=0x116` the DPCD `PAYLOAD_ALLOCATE_SET` (0x1c0) writes are

```
0x001c0 AUX <- (ret=  3) 01 69 12     # VCPI 1, start slot 0x69 = 105, 18 slots
0x001c0 AUX <- (ret=  3) 02 7b 1d     # VCPI 2, start slot 0x7b = 123, 29 slots
```

Start slots 105 and 123 are outside the 1..63 range of the MTP. The hub masks them to 6 bits (41 and 59), 59 + 29 overflows the table, and the resulting layout does not match the source's own stream encode

issues.author: Ludovico Magnocavallo
issues.description:
### Summary

On a Ryzen AI 7 350 (Krackan, Radeon 860M, gfx1152) the SMU will hold five fabric states when forced: fclk/uclk 1000/800, 1200/937, 1400/937, 1600/937 and 2000/937 (`pp_dpm_fclk` levels 1 to 7; levels 4 and 6 land on 1400 and 1600, level 0 is refused when forced but used at deep idle). ## Brief summary of the problem:
```

Disclaimer: the bug report content was generated by Claude after it helped me diagnose an issue on my own system. I am submitting it manually.

---

On a Radeon 680M (Rembrandt, DCN 3.1) running Linux 7.2, the HDMI output intermittently fails to come back when the display wakes from DPMS-off:

```
amdgpu 0000:04:00.0: [drm] enabling link 0 failed: 19        (-ENODEV)
```

It fires 1.4–2.2 s after `dpms on` and hits **\~71% of wake cycles**.

With `drm.debug=0x17` the cause is visible: **HDMI 2.1 FRL link training aborts because the sink has not asserted `FLT_READY` within the source's poll budget** -- the sink needs \~1.06 s, the source gives up sooner.

